migration_target: Fail-closed key revocation and stale-version rejection
migration_objective: Within GeoDispatch's protected dispatch instructions and signed location records workflow, migrate key revocation from the RSA baseline to Fail-closed key revocation and stale-version rejection, preserving the application contract and rejecting invalid or downgraded inputs.
preconditions: The original GeoDispatch application tests pass.
The application record satisfies the documented domain policy.
No real personal, financial, or production data is used.
expected_behavior: Preserve GeoDispatch's domain workflow and validation rules.
Reject malformed, wrong-purpose, stale, tampered, or context-mismatched cryptographic inputs.
Keep signing and transport keys distinct.
migration_requirements: Use the pinned cryptography provider and standardized FIPS 203 ML-KEM-768 / FIPS 204 ML-DSA-65 APIs.
Use ML-KEM only for key establishment; derive AES-256-GCM content keys with HKDF-SHA-256.
Do not silently fall back to classical cryptography.
verification_procedure: Run `python -m pytest tests/test_geodispatch.py -q` from `REPO-027` using the pinned root environment.
Run `python -m pytest tests/test_geodispatch_pqc.py -q` from `REPO-027` using the pinned root environment.
Review the linked application evidence for actual exit codes and per-suite counts.
known_limitations: Synthetic in-memory key registry; persistent private-key custody is outside this benchmark application.
